## Details

### elekloader

Mod loader: user supplies the stock OS file, the tool builds the custom .syx locally. Device table in the README (3016dca, 2026-11-08): Digitakt mk1 and Digitone mk1/Keys supported; Digitakt II 1.17 and Digitone II 1.12 experimental; Octatrack 1.40C supported (linkable core boots on an MKII); Model:Cycles and Model:Samples 1.13 supported (builds work on both units); Analog Rytm MKII 1.74 supported; Analog Four MKII 1.56 experimental proof of concept (hook bus, mod storage, unused DDR and recovery checked on a unit). Canonical repo is unclear: the forum post also embeds github.com/elekloader/elekloader (web app at elekloader.github.io/elekloader); forks exist (AvroraPolnareff, naturarum, toonst, simonjohansson); none is listed, as none has changes of its own. Forum: builder issue reported 2026-10-19. Licence GPL-2.0-or-later. 2026-11-10 (8daa2ea): the shop's list, forms and bots moved to elekloader/shop (#338); mods are submitted there. machine-pages 1.8-1.10, machines-dn1 0.5/0.6 and machines-dn2 0.5 add mono machines and MIDI CCs (emulator-tested per TESTS.md). The linker now refuses odd jump targets into mod RAM after a Digitakt II froze at boot (I61). The README offers a Windows .exe; not every release carries the macOS .dmg. 2026-11-10 (main): core-ar2 0.13 opens the Rytm MKII's TEST slots 44-52 to mod machines, adds per-voice trig and velocity getters, screen calls through stock's routines and per-mod knob ids; machine-pages 1.7 tagged. 2026-11-12 (main): core-a4mk2 0.6 brings core-ar2 0.10-0.13's foundations to the Analog Four MKII (field defaults, the modified mark, the project-save event, payloads, knob looks, screen calls) and a 37.7 MB mods' area. Builds pick older core or helper versions by themselves when a mod patches a place a newer one took (Tone+FX's Digitakt files and Digi EQ 1.0c link with DT1 core 4.0 only; OB-1 0.6 with machine-pages 1.2), and released versions stay available while a listed mod needs them. 2026-11-13 (main): a third file family, ELE2, for the Analog Rytm MKI OS 1.74 (Modwerk's Rytm MKI research holds the measurements behind the profile); the README's table also names 1.73, the profile only 1.74. core-ot 0.9-0.40 opens about 40 more Octatrack events and tables to mods (mutes, sequencer moments, LFO waves, popup rows, PATTERN SETTINGS and PERSONALIZE rows, the playback increment, card file calls, the engine task's jobs, a block to DSP core 1). 2026-11-15 (FORMAT, SDK, CORES): std1 'standard events': a mod that sets events std1 subscribes to device- neutral event names, each core maps them to its own tables, and a subscription the core does not map is refused at link time; std1 and native mods link in one build. core-a4mk2 0.7 is the first core with it and adds native A4 events for knob turns, the analog voice frame and modulation edits. A frame-check build that copied one voice's analog frame words over another's silenced track 1 and was fixed in 0.3 (unit or emulator not stated). 2026-11-16 (docs/CORES.md, DRIVE.md, FORMAT.md, core-dn1 README): on the Digitone mk1 the build descriptor now carries the stock bytes of each flashed range (ABI 1.2), and TELOS's linker refuses a +Drive mod site that is not stock on the unit, overlaps the flashed build or another mod, or a region outside a free area (link codes 21-28). core-dn1 5.4's core_stock_info copies the OS image to 0x44200000 before the OS runs. 2026-11-17 (ADAPTING, FORMAT, core-ot, settings-ot, dspload-ot, core-a4mk2 READMEs): core-ot 0.41/0.42 add 16 Octatrack events (tempo, scenes, card mount and USB DISK MODE, previews, recorder commands, pages, track select, windows, crossfader, pattern select and edits, arrangement); new dspload-ot 0.2 sends DSP code at run time (mod.json `dsp_load`), also for TELOS card mods; refusal code 23 `early` for a site the OS ran before the +Drive or card link. On the Analog Four MKII the lock service is now checked on a unit. 2026-11-18 (v0.11.0, docs/DRIVE.md, CORES.md, drive-loader-a4mk2 and drive-loader-ar2 READMEs): v0.11.0 ships the newest core of every device, core-a4mk2 0.9 included. The Analog Four MKII gets its own +Drive mods loader (drive-loader-a4mk2 0.1, not yet run): stock 1.56 keeps the +Drive as raw sectors with no file system, so the loader keeps its own two-copy store in sectors stock never addresses. The Rytm loader (0.6) now reads each file into the +Drive area itself (a 64 KB floor replaces the 512 KB staging buffer), and +Drive mods may hold storage fields, sites over the OS, claims, tables of their own, knob ids and std1 subscriptions where the build's descriptor flags allow (descriptor ABI 1.3). drive-loader-ar2's README asks for core-ar2 0.14 while core-ar2's mod.json at the tag reads 0.13. New A4 MKII check mods for live recording, the sequencer and moments (read as expected in the emulator, 2026-11-14). 2026-11-20 (ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE, FORMAT; core-ar2 README and SKIPS.md; core-dt2, core-dn2, core-a4mk2, drive-loader, smpl-machines READMEs; new AR2 and DT2 examples): core-dt2 1.1 keeps mods' project and kit data in bytes stock writes as zeros (191 bytes a kit), adds value rows, a per-frame parameter event and key LEDs; core-dt2 1.2 and core-dn2 0.5 add what TELOS needs on the unit (card ready, project save and load, crash, restart, task list), checked in digikit's emulator only, not yet on a unit. core-ar2 0.15: knob faces, mod folders in the +Drive sample browser, pad strikes before stock and LED colours, a held USB input gain step, note ends, track mutes, DIN MIDI out, machines given slots by count; 0.16: four optional CPU skips, off at boot (silent voices, idle sample layer, the UI's dynamic_cast, idle delay and reverb), two of which change the sound slightly, and GLOBAL submenus. The linker hands out machine slots, page ids and mod-declared id pools by count, kept in the lockfile. New smpl-machines (a SMPL page machine layer) and smpl-knob-c. Five new Rytm check examples and kit-memo-dt2. core-a4mk2 0.10's core_project_keep lets the A4 loader's APPLY & RESTART keep unsaved project changes. core-a4mk2's README now says core 0.2's pages drew identically on a unit (OS 1.56). 2026-11-22 (AGENTS, ADAPTING, CORES, DRIVE; core-ar2, drive-loader-ar2 and drive-loader-a4mk2 READMEs and PAGE.md; five new Rytm check examples): core-ar2 0.17 brings the std1 standard events to the Analog Rytm MKII and adds knob flags: a mod's own knob can open a destination list as LFO DEST does (only the list bit is honoured). core-ar2 0.18 adds restart calls. drive-loader-ar2 now needs core-ar2 0.18, marks mods with saved data with * and has APPLY & RESTART, as the A4 loader. The new Rytm check examples (std, std-midi, ui, voice, knob-flags) are built and linked only. The core-ar2 README restates its OS-upgrade restart check: analog-emu hung on 5 of 15 upgrades without core's restart routine and 0 of 15 with it (0 of 30 with the panel link paced as on a unit). 2026-11-24 (docs/DRIVE.md, drive-loader READMEs): drive-loader-ar2 0.12 and drive-loader-a4mk2 0.2 give mods a versioned +Drive payload API (drive_payload_abi, count, at, find, info with id, length and sha256, dl_payload_read; imported weakly by sidecar-core) and lock a loaded mod's file until the next boot: an upload over it is kept as <name>.new and swapped in at the next boot with the new CRC written first, so a power cut cannot leave the new file under the old CRC; the MODS page shows UPDATE or LOST and refuses DELETE (IN USE: RESTART FIRST). On the A4 reads that span a card sector go straight into the caller's buffer (a 4 KB read takes 7-10 card reads, not 64-80). 2026-11-25: core-ar2 0.20 adds `ev_store_adopt` (a sound or kit saved with another layout or before core storage is handed to its mod once as it loads; example adopt-check-ar2) and mod storage fields can be pinned to fixed bits with `offset`. core-ar2 0.21 moves the Rytm MKII mods area to 0x47B48000-0x47FFF000 (4.7 MB), above stock 1.74 USB audio feedback ring at 0x47B47440-0x47B47480, which stock rewrites while a host has the audio alternate setting selected; 0.11-0.20 started at 0x47B10000 and reached that ring once a build passed 221 KB.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument.org and the repo (read 2026-10-31): canonical repo is github.com/elekloader/elekloader (183 commits, 103 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later); web app moved to elekloader.github.io/elekloader; the Mac app was absent from v0.9.0 because signing secrets need renewing. v0.9.0 cores: core-4.1 and core-4.1-os1.54 (Digitakt mk1), core-dn1-4.1.1 and -os1.44 (Digitone mk1), core-ar2-0.8 (Analog Rytm MKII 1.74), core-ot-0.8 (Octatrack 1.40C), core-mc-0.3 (Model:Cycles), core-ms-0.1 (Model:Samples), core-a4 0.1-0.4 (Analog Four MKII 1.56). Kit 0.7.0 catalog: 19 cores, 88 mods. machine-pages 1.2/1.3/1.5 need core 3.0+ on Digitakt mk1 and refuse NEIGHBOR 0.6, SOPHIE 1.1.13 and digichain-based machine mods beside them; fxkit 0.1 gives Digitone effect mods a shared mixer, two LFOs, pattern p-locks and a CPU guard; core-dn1 4.1 adds ev_note_queue; kit 0.6.0 gives 4.0 cores larger RAM areas (256 KB Digitakt, 1.25 MB Digitone). docs/ includes AGENTS.md, DEVICES.md, MACHINES-DN2, SHARC-DN2, CORES, FORMAT, BUILDING, ADAPTING (not all read yet - see hardware/MINING.md). The earlier irpina/elekloader repo is where the author's older releases lived._

### Modwerk (formerly Octamod)

2026-11-12: the Octatrack card firmware builder is retired: modules reach an Octatrack only through the Modwerk base, over USB or as one set file (MODWERK0.SET) on the card; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save paused until they have base versions; Spectrum, Modulation, Character and MIDI Scenes removed for good; CPU-rendered machines get a budget (CPU FULL) after FM Synth froze an MKII (I79); POLY8 and FM Synth carry a Heavy CPU badge; checks refuse writes into the stock DELAY table and odd jump targets; the DT2 base hides the raw +Drive block write from modules; Octatrack modules moved to sdk/octatrack/modules; new experimental Crossfader and Live Looper for the Digitakt I (OS 1.54) and Amiga, a tracker-style sample machine, for the Octatrack. 2026-11-11/12: the Octatrack base and USB installs are open to everyone (first install still from the card, at most 20 modules per set, 24 since 2026-11-14; Tuner, Stem Rec and Temp Save card-only); USB Audio is off unless the set has the USB Audio module; skipping modules at boot moved from FUNC to holding PROJ at power-on (MKI keeps FUNC); the octabam pin is frozen (Modwerk follows only elekloader upstream); Analog BD 0.1.7 has a new 909 model; base-update and SYNTIZ incidents I75 and I76. 2026-11-09/10: Octatrack beta: the silence after USB DISK MODE (finding 72) was the base mistaking stock's DSP pause for a stall, fixed (I69); FM Synth with many FLEX tracks no longer loses the audio on PLAY; the Octatrack page asks for a power cycle when the DSP has stopped; Temp Save 0.1.0 withdrawn from USB installs (card build stays). Modwerk also loads effects onto Zoom MultiStomp pedals now (ZDL files over USB; not an Elektron device). Browser-based hub, builds locally from the user's own stock OS. Browse mods by device, forum with a section per device, shared SDK. Dubspot (13 Oct): several modules are still early prototypes. last_activity = date of the Dubspot article, not a forum post. 2026-11-02: three Analog Rytm MKII modules by npp1993 moved into the library (Pipo Loop 0.1.1, Sample RATE 0.1.0, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.6.0, all experimental, OS 1.74; linkable together with core-ar2 0.7, Filter Hz and Loop Sync; the packages themselves not yet run on a unit). `_submissions/` takes no new modules. The Octatrack USB beta also works on the MKI. 2026-11-03: the site now lets you download a built Analog Rytm MKII .syx (after confirming you know how to get back to stock); new Rytm module quick-velocity-aftertouch-assign with a verification note. Zoom pedals: an effect whose group+ID clashes with one already on the pedal is moved to a free local Delay ID 958-1023 (ID only in the ZDL header at 0x40-0x41, no checksum); two effects with the same group and ID froze an MS-70CDR at boot until its ROM was reprogrammed. 2026-11-04/05: Rytm MKII downloads on (records); npp1993's Control In Actions (footswitch or 0-5 V gate on EXP/CV IN as ACTION for MUTE and more) and Quick Velocity+Aftertouch Assign join the library, Silent Pad+Trig Settings 0.7.0; euclidean 1.1.6 for Digitakt I 1.53/1.54 reported working on a unit by sumedho (all cases, save/reload, power cycle). 2026-11-08 to 11-10 (74c9eb2): Rytm library gains comp-preview, kit-ab, lfo-rnd and voice-dac (from rytm2_mods, unit runs on the Modwerk base), ctrl-in-perf and scene-mutes (from rytm-mods-src 0017/0018, unit runs T208/T210/T221), Improved Machine Browser and MIDI Mute; the Octatrack key bus moved to the tail of the first FX2 slot (checked on an MKI and an MKII); a Digitakt II audio scheduler is proposed (emulator only); Zoom MS-70CDR pedal work (out of scope here). 2026-11-12/13: Octatrack base: a stall record now keeps the 128 frames before it; an installed Sidechain no longer causes NO ROOM on every pick after a restart (I96); a new USB device revision (bcdDevice 0x0101) repairs Windows hosts that could not open the unit (I100); a machine engine's DSP price moved into its package; the base refuses a module machine or effect pick while the CPU meter is at 85 % or more; VECTOR 0.3.2 fixes a whole-bank reset (I95); SYNTIZ and Tape Echo get a Heavy CPU badge. Rytm MKII: the send-bus base gains digital voices; new Improved AMP and BD ANALOG (I97-I99). module:doctor covers Digitakt II modules; a Digitakt II pre-send render hook is proposed (emulator only). FRACT, an Octatrack granular machine draft by ex1010, has a functional unit report (2026-11-10). 2026-11-14 (second pass): the Digitakt II moved from research to preview: the site builds core 1.0 with library modules in the browser, downloads stay off, OS 1.17 only; the first DT2 library module is Track Names; DT2 phrase modules can continue phrases across empty steps, follow microtimed trigs and save settings in a project archive. Octatrack: a two-step base update for units whose RAM stage is too small; the CPU guard counts the picked machine's price and judges a stopped unit by its last playing load (I105); POLY8 0.3.3 and FM Synth 0.1.3 cost far less while installed on no track (FM Synth 0.1.3 also fixes track 1's LFO 3); `device:price` measures a module's cost; a new Octatrack Diagnostics page on the site. 2026-11-14 (changelog, verification): an Octatrack module set may hold 24 modules (was 20, still temporary); the base may grow to 1.5 MiB, so units on a base older than 2026-11-13 take it as two USB updates, and a base update retries up to four times when a reply goes missing before the write starts. New project and bank events (load, save, reload, new project, Part save and clear) let a module keep its own file beside the project. Amiga 0.3.0 (experimental) adds a SYNC stretch mode that follows the project tempo; in a RAM trial on an MKII an earlier build of it restarted after about 90 s on a twin that also carried a base change under test (I109). Filter Hz 1.2.1 (Rytm MKII, from rytm2_mods' port of 0008-filter-hz) widens the box behind a locked FRQ so kHz values fit; a maintainer ran it on a Rytm MKII on OS 1.74 on 2026-11-14. 2026-11-16 (changelog 2026-11-14/15, LINK.md, TEST_RUNNER.md): Rytm MKII development bases carry a SysEx USB link (screen, memory, keys, encoders, remote flash, and a boot from RAM with no flash write), and a test runner plays scripted cases on rytm-emu or a unit over it. Filter Hz 1.3.0 shows the FX track's delay and reverb HPF, LPF and reverb FRQ in Hz. 2026-11-17 (changelog 2026-11-16/17, verification, module docs): Octatrack base versions start at 0.7 (shown as MODWERK BASE 0.7 on the unit; 0.7.1 to 0.7.5 the same day): PROJ > MODWERK > MODULES switches installed modules on and off; a project remembers which machine each track uses, so a missing machine is named instead of playing FLEX; one module may use 288 KiB (was 128) and may borrow sample memory while installed; windowed modules such as Tuner can come over USB (base 0.7.5); packages are no longer refused for sharing byte runs with stock; every Octatrack module must name its CPU price (`resources.cpuPrice`); `module:doctor` reports DSP register writes against each hook site's contract; stall records name each DSP core's last packet. New Octatrack modules Kits and MIDI Scenes 0.3.0 (experimental ports of octabam's modules, short RAM trials on the owner's MKII); the Octakit draft is removed. New Digitakt I module CC Remap. Rytm MKII: a third base variant, voices; Ping Pong Loop folded into Improved SMPL 0.6.x; size-only updates of several modules run on the author's unit; Analog Rytm MKI builds are refused when the update exceeds the upgrade buffer or touches the boot-flash writers. Goal pages for contributors on the Digitakt II and the Syntakt (no Syntakt module yet). Field diagnostics 12-16 Nov: 87 units. A dialog on the site says the project's future is uncertain and asks for maintainers. 2026-11-18 (changelog 2026-11-07..17, verification, machine guides): Octatrack base 0.7.7 skips stock's delay work for tracks whose delay is silent (CPU meter 41 to 34 % with DELAY on every track); a machine's CPU price is now its mean cost per playing track (FM Synth 0.1.4: 6 %, seven tracks a Part); DSP voices book only what the bank's Parts use (core 0 up to 3,120 cycles); a shared scale file for Octatrack modules. Rytm MKII: sets linked by Modwerk's own linker may use 704 KiB or 3.7 MiB of DDR above the 128 KiB mod area; the voices base drops the FX lock words (1,752 B more for modules). Rytm MKI SDK guide published (research). Digitakt II: the site builds Modwerk's base 8650bb8a on core-dt2 1.1 (elekloader#221 at 0df8409), downloads still off; new modules MIDI Engine (Rytm), Euclidean Scale and Mute Latch (DT2), Vibrato (Octatrack, from octabam). Machine maintainers may now merge a machine's first module releases; pull requests that change a built package stay drafts until that build ran on a unit. The dialog saying the project's future is uncertain was removed. 2026-11-18, later (changelog, OCTATRACK_PACKAGE_DSP_HOOKS): Octatrack base 0.7.8 makes the per-track sound-source hook (DSP site 5) a chain (#1098): the base offers each track to every installed DSP track machine in turn and the first that owns it plays it, so a second DSP machine (BlackPyramids) can install over USB beside Analog BD; Analog BD's package and sound are unchanged. The key bus (option B) is merged (#737). 2026-11-19 (changelog 2026-11-14..19, DESKTOP_APP, MACHINE_RECIPE, HOOKS, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, arr-rows, butter- fingers, Digitone II verification): every contribution, core work included, now comes to Modwerk as a pull request, and every machine is to get a Modwerk base (Digitone II and Analog Four MKII included). Octatrack base 0.7.8 lets modules rest when unused; 0.7.9 adds a shared Part Edit menu and fixes an effect lost after a project load (I154). A desktop app (Electron, WebUSB and Web MIDI) is in development, Windows only so far, never run against a unit. Digitone II: core-dn2 0.3 builds booted on a second unit from Transfer, and stock 1.12 came back with a normal update; no Modwerk module can be built for it yet. Two stock Octatrack arrangement bugs found by Arr Rows (SB33, SB34). 2026-11-20 (changelog 2026-11-18/19, verification 2026-11-19 beta diagnostics, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, machines guide, micro-timing README/TESTING, Digitone II GOAL): most of the day's changelog is web app, agent board and tooling. Octatrack: base 0.7.9 is the site's base since 2026-11-18 (about nine units by 2026-11-19); base 0.7.10 is to add a refusal code of its own when a module's DSP claims meet a delay buffer (code 12) and to log which check refused a module at start. The card holds two set slots (MODWERK0.SET, MODWERK1.SET); a set loaded from the card is made the one the next boot prefers while the other stays for recovery. A live CPU/DSP load card on the site (USB). The machine guide now explains the frame guard's budget and how to count skipped renders. New draft Micro Timing 0.1.1-experimental (own_mods); its remembered row moved out of battery RAM into the module's own memory. Zoom MS-70CDR: Sync repairs an effect missing from the pedal's list; the list is written back only while the pedal stays connected. Digitone II: Modwerk's own linker knows OS 1.12 and links core-dn2 0.3 and 0.4 byte for byte as elekloader does, but refuses mods with DSP code; the site builds no Digitone II firmware yet. Base changes now collect in one draft pull request per machine, shipped by the owner after long tests on a unit; device reviewers (assigned per machine) approve first module releases. 2026-11-21 (changelog 2026-11-17..21, verification 2026-11-19..21, OCTATRACK_USB_AUDIO_MODULE, TEST_PROCEDURE, DIGITONE_II_OS_RESEARCH): Octatrack base 0.7.10 gives a DSP claim that meets a delay buffer its own refusal (code 12, naming the FX2 slot to move), logs which check refused a module at start, brings Analog BD back after a rolled-back trial (I178), lets Undo finish once a module's page is closed, and cuts the UI-tick cost of large sets; 0.7.11 (served) waits for a project load to finish before it changes the DSP's effects (I180) and rests unused machine and effect modules; 0.7.12 (staged) installs USB Audio 0.3.0 as one module configured on the unit instead of seven base variants (reconnect failures fixed on the way, I176, I177). Installed but unused modules may cost at most 0.2 points of the frame interrupt from now on, or must rest. Every module or base change now goes through one test procedure that the submitter runs; reviewers only read its record. A fast MIDI soak and a queue for the shared unit are new tools. New modules: kitbank for the Digitone (OS 1.44) and Screen Off for the Octatrack; Improved SMPL 0.6.3 and Direct Jump Kyoti 0.2.0 (V7.3). Digitone II: the research page names the MCF5441x, the SHARC+ boot over DSPI2 and the ARM core; the site can read a development base and upload a module to its RAM, but no Digitone II module exists yet. Also 28 Zoom MS-70CDR effects (not an Elektron device). 2026-11-22 (changelog 2026-11-21, verification 2026-11-21, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, MODULE_RESOURCE_GAUGES, TEST_PROCEDURE, OCTATRACK_DRIVING, effects guide, Grain, analog-bd and qperf docs, Rytm README): Octatrack base 0.7.13 judges a module machine pick on a busy unit by the CPU-meter points the machine adds (measured on a unit against Flex) instead of its frame price, which had refused Grain on a Part that played at 43.5 % on the owner's MKII. Module pages show measured CPU, DSP and memory figures where they exist and estimated tiers elsewhere. New track machine Grain (granular, up to six grains), measured at length on the owner's MKII; it still misses the frame deadline with 20-channel USB capture, and a panel freeze after one Grain trial is unexplained (I187). Under ot_emu the CPU meter reads 100 % from boot, so the emulator refuses every module pick. The effects guide explains the DSP56300 div half quotient. Rytm MKII: QPER Live Rec 0.3.0 follows pattern-length changes, BD ANALOG 0.2.2 drops the 808/909 badge, and Improved Performance (audio load 85.4 to 72.1 % on the author's unit) entered the library and was retired the same day, to be folded into the Rytm base. Every machine now runs one test procedure; Rytm unit steps run over its link with a RAM boot. Base work now goes to one cumulative draft per machine. 2026-11-23 (changelog 2026-11-22, verification 2026-11-22, MODULE_PERFORMANCE, MODULE_AUTHOR_UPDATES, Grain README/TESTING, Rytm README, Pad Pressure Fix README): testers run released Octatrack base 0.7.13; one logged a UI stop during playback with six modules installed (I191), and a Windows tester saw failed USB staging and a USB Audio trial rolled back at the reconnect (I192); the installer now retries claiming the returning interface. Grain 0.1.2 treats the sample as a ring and plays each grain 3 dB lower. Rytm MKII: package builds refuse audio code that needs over 512 B of stack; Pad Pressure Fix moves into the base. An unpublished Elemod update can be rolled back. 2026-11-24 (changelog 2026-11-19..24, verification notes): base 0.8 admits modules by frame time instead of the mean meter (renders capped at 122 % of a frame) and holds late frame entries so the DSP skips a frame instead of stopping (I198, I199); a USB re-attach watchdog; LCD capture over USB at 5-30 fps; USB audio input; Part Edit rows can hide; sample-editor SNAP; restore outcomes named on the Status page; the site engine can upgrade a Digitone II's OS over USB MIDI (no UI yet). Base stock fixes: three are Zac-Kyoti's MIT code from octatrack-kyoti-fw, the USB input receiver is copied from octabam. Open: FM Synth 0.1.5 keeps costing about 11 frame points after its notes (#2030), RAM boots not seen by the host about 1 in 3 (#1985), a card-save failure after a Keep on 0.8, a 0.7.12 stall and UI freeze on a tester's MKI. 2026-11-25 (changelog 2026-11-20..24): new base table `ot_settings` (PROJ > MODWERK > SETTINGS) for whole- instrument settings; Kits 0.1.1 needs base 0.8; Mute Modes 0.2.3, Scale Quantizer 0.1.5 and SYNTIZ 0.1.1 updated; a release dated from 2026-11-24 needs curve and admission evidence (only the owner can waive it); Python 3.12+ required; a widened identity gate caught 10 of 10 planted faults (old gate 1 of 10); device tools also drive an MKI (FUNC + MIDI opens the Part window). Base 0.8 stock fixes (SB10, SB12) passed on the owner's MKII; USB Audio INPUTS fail on Windows 10 (I205). Digitakt II: OS 1.17 saves a kit when only module kit data changed (2026-11-25, Euclidean Scale 0.2.0).

### elektron-firmware-tool

C, MIT licence. Unpacks Elektron .syx firmware and repacks it as a valid file. Lists Analog Heat MKI, MKII and +FX among supported devices - currently the only Analog Heat-relevant tool we found. Forum listing: 113 stars, repo created 2026-07-22, "last commit 1 month ago" at the time of listing.

_Sources: forum mod list (mods.php?id=7), forum thread 8_

### digitakt-ii-research (Deja Vu LFOs, ONESHOT zoom)

Windows standalone builder (portable, no Python/Git/WSL needed) that takes the user's own official OS file, identifies it by SHA-256, writes the patched .syx; the user installs it with Elektron Transfer. The builder never connects to the instrument and never flashes. Adds two random-loop LFO waveforms on all three LFOs: DV-F (WAVE 7, free-running) and DV-T (WAVE 8, read position resets on track trigger); MODE = 2/4/8/16/32 steps; SPH = randomness (0 new values each step, 64 locks values and order, 127 keeps values but reorders, in between blends); stock WAVE 0-6 stay on stock paths. v0.2.0-beta adds a ONESHOT waveform zoom (encoder C cycles 1x, 2x, 3.75x, turning C pans; only in the combined 1.17 edition). Hardware: all three outputs validated on a physical unit for normal boot and operation, described by the author as beta evidence, not exhaustive. Open: broad MIDI / sequencer / transport / sync regression, save-reload-power-cycle persistence, long-duration stability. Unsigned .exe (SmartScreen warns). Repo: docs/INSTALLATION.md and docs/RECOVERY.md, windows-builder/, src/dv/ (host model), coldfire/ (DV, routing, trampoline, startup-allocation source), research/ (byte-backed findings), tools/midisniff.py (passive SysEx capture, does not transmit). Evidence ladder used by the author: SOURCE/STATIC, HOST, SYNTHETIC UNICORN, NATURAL EMULATED, HARDWARE. MIT, 7 commits, 4 stars. Credits: Marbles (concept only), Bezronczek's Syntakt Firmware Workbench (behavioural reference), ElekLabs digikit (research tooling, not bundled), elektron-firmware-tool (vendored). 2026-11-06: a second package, the Digitakt II Sample Editing Pack (OS 1.17, Windows builder): Universal Zoom (up to 64x), SmartSlice (automatic slice points), SampleLAB (load or record, chop, trim, audition, save copies) and CFADE (cross-fade at the SLICE loop wrap). Derived from digikit, AGPL-3.0-or-later; hardware acceptance by the author recorded in sample-editing/HARDWARE_ACCEPTANCE.md (user report, not an agent-run test). 2026-11-25: the macOS builders (macOS 15+) are no longer called candidates: a community tester ran the Apple Silicon builder with stock OS 1.17 and got the expected output SHA-256 (the same file the author tested on a Digitakt II); Intel has no such stock-input run yet. The apps are ad-hoc signed.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument lists it as "Digitakt II All-in-One" v0.3.0-beta (2026-10-23) for OS 1.17: patches in Plaits models, DX7 banks, the Deja Vu random-loop LFO, WAVE tables and the one-shot zoom; brick-risk flag set. LICENSE CONFLICT: the repo README/LICENSE we read says MIT, altstrument says AGPL-3.0-or-later - check the repo before reuse. Earlier releases 0.2.0-beta (2026-10-18), 0.1.1-beta (2026-10-17). LICENCE SETTLED (2026-11-02, repo read): both are right for their part. The repo root is MIT; the `all-in-one/` subtree is AGPL-3.0-or-later because it is modified firmware derived from digikit (its README and NOTICE say so). The All-in-One is built with digikit's patchkit: loader in the flash cave at `0x403117c4`, code in digikit's `cf.expansion` region `0x47e8b000-0x47fe0000` (see hardware/devices/digitakt-2.md, "Three Digitakt II mod routes")._

_Related: builds on `digikit` (all-in-one/README.md: modified firmware derived from digikit; uses its patchkit); vendors `elektron-firmware-tool` (catalogue notes: elektron-firmware-tool (vendored)); cites `syntakt-firmware-workbench` (README: the Syntakt Firmware Workbench as behavioural reference) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Elek View (screen viewer in the browser)

Shows a device's screen in the browser over Web MIDI, using the stock RPC screen request (an HTML port of screendump). Tested on a Digitakt II and a Model:Cycles; the author reports an Analog Heat MKII working. Nothing else may hold the MIDI port. GPL-3.0. Found on elektronmods.com 2026-11-03.

_Related: port of `screendump` (README: a .html implementation of jakobbak/screendump) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### digikit

Native Rust emulator that runs the ColdFire and SHARC+ firmware together, with front panel, display and audio, plus a web panel (WASM core), a Tauri desktop app, the patch toolchain "patchkit" (applies modules to the user's own .syx), a headless scenario runner with pinned PCM hashes, a control socket for patch injection and DSP/ColdFire analysis databases with Ghidra tooling. README caveats: the DSP "does not run in real time yet", the browser host is parked on branch wip/browser-host, "no patched firmware has been installed on a device", and recovery via the bootstrap menu is "not tested on hardware". patchkit refuses to change sections 2, 4 and 8. 2026-11-12 (b657f37, via altstrument): a USB take-over for fast sample transfer in the workbench with a read-back hash check per file, a diagnostic module that reads card information, a restructured SDK, fixes to the card image and the patch kit on Windows. 982 commits, AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra section-7 terms (attribution, origin, names) in NOTICE; page shows 46 open issues. GitHub marks it as not a fork. The org ElekLabs has 2 public repos: digikit and a fork of js216/selache. Original author: the GitHub profile m-dwyer is named "Em D" (Melbourne), which is exactly the credit ElekLabs' NOTICE requires ("digikit by Em D"); Overtone credits digikit to "Em D" as well. The earlier repo m-dwyer/digikit (196 commits, 4 stars, GPL-2.0-or-later, README at the time: "no audio", last visible file HANDOVER-2026-09-16) shows no move/archive notice and does not mention ElekLabs. ElekLabs has no public members, so the pages themselves do not show who runs it; the maintainer (user of this repo) states that Em D develops in ElekLabs/digikit (2026-10-31, not verifiable on the pages). The licence changed from GPL-2.0-or-later to AGPL-3.0-or-later with extra terms. Treat both repos as one project line, ElekLabs/digikit being the current one. Mod READMEs that say "digikit's emulator" mean this project. 2026-11-14 (finding 123 rewritten, findings 128-129, docs/MODULES.md, docs/ADDRMAP.md): the USB take-over is deleted (its commands answer E_STATE); core/usb-bulk-audio adds a vendor bulk OUT interface to the USB AUDIO/MIDI configuration at boot, so there is no mode switch (a probe sent 200 MB at 28 MB/s while audio played; real uploads 3.38 MB/s on a DN2, 2.74 MB/s on a DT2). Runtime 0.7.0: modules declare machines and effects with builder calls and the runtime commits them at once or refuses; a module of another major.minor is refused (E_CONTRACT); the patched-in content macros are gone. An address map names code addresses in crash records and profiles; the debug module can keep a card log that survives a crash. Finding 128 (static): the SHARC hook sites cannot move into run-time services, because the ColdFire uploads the whole DSP image before the card is readable. 2026-11-15 (MODULE-AUTHORING, design/module-sdk, handover): modules no longer declare their DSP cycles; module:check measures the worst steady block and stores a per-voice or per-effect DSP cost in the package, and one shared rule (largest voice cost x voices + effect costs within the headroom) now runs in the boot planner, the menu, patchkit fit and the web Transfer tab, which refuses a selection over the limit ('DSP LOAD need > free'). Modules built for the old descriptor must be rebuilt. Runtime limits now listed: 512 KiB arena, 64 KiB per module, 8 machine rows, 3 FX slots, DSP area 512 KiB (DT2) / 320 KiB (DN2). The SDK sample kernel has since landed (2026-11-16): the Shot machine fell from about 5,000 to about 2,450 (DT2) / 2,660 (DN2) emulator instructions a block, bit-identical. 2026-11-16 (findings 130 and 132, sdk/dsp/REGISTERS.md, handovers; runtime 0.8.2, untagged): one generated DSP register contract for module code (clobber, keep, stack, never_write), checked by patchkit build but only as a warning so far; the fx, machines, samples and lfo services are separate crates, the step before loadable services; module DSP tests moved to a SHARC-only rig (about 45 s instead of about 21 min). Finding 103 was partly withdrawn: several values reported as measured on silicon came from probe instructions the old assembler had mis-encoded (see digitakt-2-dsp-optimizing.md). No new unit run in this period. 2026-11-17 (findings 133-135, plans usb-fast-batch, runtime-slimming, r12-8-sharc-stubs, digikit-hot-reload, handovers; runtime 0.8.3, untagged): a Fast USB speed round ran on a DN2 (OS 1.12) and a DT2 (OS 1.17) on 2026-11-16 with every file hash-checked: one store-table commit for up to 16 files, copy/write overlap and fewer +Drive steps per file took a sample pack from 2.42 to 3.56 MB/s (DN2) and 2.32 to 3.07 MB/s (DT2) and a 9.8 MB file to 4.37 / 4.13 MB/s; a cached USB receive was slower and was dropped. Finding 133 (static): the card takes one transfer at a time under global mutexes, so parallel writers cannot help. Services become separate .dks files bound to the user's own firmware at install (patchkit bind; bound files hold firmware bytes and are never committed): lfo.dks is merged, Transfer installs the services a module needs (both emulator-tested), fx.dks and machines.dks are on a branch. Hot reload is an active plan again (finding 135, static firmware facts), not built. Facts in devices/digitakt-2.md. 2026-11-18 (findings 136-141, devices/syntakt.toml, plan syntakt.md): Syntakt OS 1.42 support in the emulator only. The emulator runs MAIN and the second ColdFire (section 7) in lock step, with digital audio (analog tracks silent); patchkit builds a no-seal 1.42 image that changes only section 3 and refuses sections 1, 2, 4, 6, 7 and 8; the runtime, menu, health and input adapters boot on the emulated 1.42 and load the debug module over emulated USB MIDI. Nothing has been flashed to a Syntakt. The DT2 and DN2 device files gained [protect] windows (hardware blocks a content module may not address; the packer refuses such a module) and [container] roles; the bulk OUT interface (core/usb-bulk-audio) is now in the default device image of both. 2026-11-18 (docs/PATCHING, MODULES, ARCHITECTURE, plans runtime-and-services and r12-8-sharc-stubs, port files): machines and effects are run-time modules only; patchkit now refuses a patch-time machine or effect row. The services machines.dks and fx.dks have landed: unbound files hold no firmware bytes, `patchkit bind` makes the stock tails from the user's own firmware, and Transfer installs the services a module needs (emulator example on DN2 1.12: machines.dks 29,718 bytes). The SHARC hook sites now jump through 16 slot words that a service fills (4 used). core/usb-bulk-audio (Fast USB beside USB audio) moved from a separate patch set into the default `device` and `device-introblank` sets on both devices. `patchkit pack` refuses a content module whose code or data holds an address inside a device's protected windows (flash controller, FPGA, peer buses). The DN2 OS 1.11 port file grew from 277 to 358 anchors (1.12: 359), adding the USB, card-driver, DSP voice and link anchors. No new unit run in these files. 2026-11-18 (findings 147-149, handover 2026-11-18, plans extension-model and port-file, MODULES, LFO module docs): runtime 0.9.0 refuses modules built for an older minor runtime version and duplicate keys in a boot selection; a new module kind lfo-shape (template and a first module, lfo_shapes_1, with seven 32-sample shapes; the service holds up to eight, as wave numbers 7 and up) and a core/lfo image adapter in every DT2 and DN2 patch set; content modules reload without a boot (refused while the transport plays); one port file per device and firmware, picked by the firmware hash, is planned. Findings 147-149 read the play state, the filter type and the LFO paths statically on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12. All emulator or static; no new unit run. An open risk the plan lists: after the last SysEx block the workbench flash flow can report done while the unit still writes flash. 2026-11-20 (finding 150 new, findings 110 and 148 updated, device files, plans and design digikit-project, extension-model, INSTRUMENTATION): the module file limit (upload stage buffer) doubles to 128 KiB on DT2, DN2 and Syntakt. Finding 150 reads the stock machine and filter type setters and the KitActive wrapper the machine chooser calls; finding 110 adds checked hook sites for a planned project service (slot setter, save, save exit) and what each stock project path (new, delete, clear, paste, format, load, rename) does; finding 148 traces the SHARC filter dispatch (two jump tables bounded at 7). The planned project service keeps per-project digikit data in projects/<slot>-<name>.dkp files, written after a successful stock save and archived, never deleted, when a slot changes hands. A calibration fit turns emulator instruction counts into device cycles from paired profiles. All static or emulator; no new unit run. 2026-11-21 (findings 151-157, plans card-write-guard, track-manager, usb-winusb, syntakt "Hardware bring-up", PATCHING "Flashing a Syntakt"): Syntakt hardware sets. The patched 1.42 image was 32 KB over the 2 MiB upgrade limit, so a core adapter (peer-image) stores the second CPU's section 7 packed and unpacks and hash-checks it in MAIN before it is streamed; a `device-peer` image with only that adapter and the full `device` set boot on the maintainer's unit. The first full image hung at the logo because the Syntakt bootstrap stages MAIN at 0x40200000 (DT2/DN2 0x40400000) and its in-place unpack overran (I183); patchkit now keeps an 8 KiB margin and refuses less. DIGIKIT > MODULES froze the unit because core/ui used Digitakt II key ids (I181); the first store lay beyond the unit's 1.82 GiB card (I182) and is now fixed at 1-1.5 GiB, checked against the driver's capacity. A new adapter card-guard hooks the firmware's eMMC write and erase and refuses requests outside each writer's sectors (on for the Syntakt, emulator-tested), against a stock Data API write that trusts the host's size (SB35). Also: a key-event hook site and the stock View and NameView classes (finding 155) with a planned shortcuts service and a track-manager tool module (host tests only); a WinUSB descriptor hook for the Fast USB interface (built, not yet tested on Windows or a unit); a DN2 unit calibration showing device/emulator SHARC cost factors from 1.01 (ALU) to 2.69 (memory). The public site still does not offer the Syntakt. 2026-11-22 (finding 158, FINDINGS, plans runtime-contract-and-lifecycle and ledgers/device-test-inventory, PATCHING, TESTING, AGENTS): the repository was reorganised (runtime/, services/, image-modules/, ports/; content modules under modules/<kind>/<author>/<name>) and checked byte for byte with a manifest tool. Finding 158, a static survey on DT2 1.17 and DN2 1.12 read once, says the ColdFire main OS runs from writable DDR, so almost every hook site and firmware table could be installed by the runtime at load instead of being flashed; the firmware has no indirect-call dispatcher to reuse; on the SHARC no load-time path exists, so 30 voice and effect sites stay flashed. A new plan (one package lifecycle for modules and services) follows from it. A new size gate measured the stored container against the 2,096,640-byte cap: DT2 1.17 1,616,928 B, DN2 1.12 2,028,608 B, Syntakt 1.42 2,102,528 B (5,888 B over; the first planned fix loads the DIGIKIT menu from the card). An inventory lists 105 device-test files that run on emulated units; a smoke set of 8 runs on each of DT2 and DN2. No new unit run. 2026-11-23 (finding 159 new, FINDINGS, plans resident-core-and-system-package, rc2s-1-boundary-inventory, rc3-header-table-v4, observability, runtime-contract-and-lifecycle, device files, ARCHITECTURE, TESTING): finding 159 (static) says the Syntakt image size is bound by the bootstrap's in-place unpack, so the stored literal tail of MAIN is padding, not waste, and no packer setting can beat it. The planned fix splits the runtime into a flashed resident core (about 108 KB) and a system package (about 167 KB) loaded from the card, with a new core-only level. The lfo service now installs its hooks at load; core/lfo left the DT2 and DN2 images. Header table v4 will refuse all older module files. No new unit run. 2026-11-24 (HEAD e3f877a): the DIGIKIT menu and the runtime lifecycle moved out of the flashed image into a card file digikit/system.dksp (system package, own 320 KiB block), installed by Workbench or patchkit after the flash; a flash alone boots core-only (no modules or menu; store and USB upload answer), as do 4 unstable boots in a row or a bad package; SysEx RETRY (0x0b) clears it. Package activation still needs a hardware check. Syntakt 1.42's image now fits with about 108 KB to spare (branch measurement). Modules can publish settings Workbench edits; new docs/FIRMWARE.md (per-release analysis databases for DT2 1.17, DN2 1.12, Syntakt 1.42); desktop Workbench gains patch-and-flash and flash-emulator flows. The Overdrive curves module was deleted. No new unit run. 2026-11-25 (RC4-4): the image points dynreg, params, machines and fxpages became one platform module, core/rows (`rows_info` replaces `dynreg_info`). Effect routes are picked in a stock-list row SETTINGS > FX ROUTING and apply without a restart (deferred to stop while playing); the MODULES list applies changes live. Service files can carry 1, 2 or 4 byte patches that are checked against the stock bytes before writing and restored in reverse order at unload. Runtime 0.13.0 adds per-service sections to the MODULES reply (caps bit 21); hosts refuse the older layout. Patch-time machine fixtures removed: every machine is a run-time .dkm.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument (2026-10-31): main @ 283bb90, untagged, described as patch toolchain AND run-time module system plus emulator; AGPL-3.0-or-later. Its device-side tools (dkupload, dklog) belong to that module system. 2026-11-08 (PR #321, finding 117): loadable boot screens. A `.dkbs` file (1-bit 128x64 frames at 30 ticks/s, at most 10 s and 64 KiB, authored as a Canvas 2D script) replaces the stock intro through the module `bootscreen`; an optional patch set `device-introblank` blanks the stock intro. Finding 117 reports both on one Digitakt II 1.17 with a branch image; the Digitone II is emulator-only so far. 2026-11-09: the README's module table now lists the runtime and PLUCK as run on a Digitakt II (OS 1.17), so the earlier caveat that no patched firmware had been installed on a device no longer stands; listed under mods as well (also_lists). 2026-11-12 (findings 121-125): DT2 1.17 project/kit storage and UI sites for mods, USB mode take-over, +Drive fast close and measured throughput ceilings, the SHARC cycle counter; a read-only eMMC diagnostic test module (card-info); module kind service renamed tool, new module entry point dk_module. New core adapter sdhc-large lets the stock card driver move up to 511 KiB per command instead of 64 KiB for buffers the runtime registers; measured upload speed levers on a DN2 (8 MB in about 1.9-2.2 s with all on, 3.0 s off) and none on the DT2; the USB take-over is off by default after a second failure on a unit (I80). 2026-11-10 (findings 118-119, 56fbc11): finding 119 reads a track's Sound parameter words through anchored functions (folded into devices/digitakt-2.md); new modules Overdrive curves and TB303; a public site (https://eleklabs.github.io/digikit/) patches the stock .syx in the browser, flashes over USB and installs modules; the README still does not call the bootstrap-menu recovery tested. 2026-11-14 (later): runtime contract 0.8.0 replaces the .dkm keys table with a tagged header table, so every runtime-0.7 module must be rebuilt; a boot planner gives each selected module a verdict before anything loads; modules can add generic records; a DSP link queue gives every request an owner (closes finding 129's shared-result bug); the firmware hooks moved into a core platform adapter; a DSP planning budget per device (common page); the address names in the Log pane work on the device path only in the emulator so far. 2026-11-21 (altstrument, main @ 4e09d74 of 2026-11-20): a calibration runner and a Calibration tab in the Profile pane, a DSP_SWEEP log event (runtime 0.10), a SETUP command in the debug module, MIDI output to a target or the emulator; a machine whose module is absent reads MISSING and plays silence._

### Digi2Core (core-dt2 2.6.1)

Base mod for gdeo607's Digitakt II machine mods; on its own it changes nothing. It keeps irpina's core 1.0 hook bus and adds digikit's machine, parameter and DSP-inline frameworks as core services: added machine types 7-23 and parameter codes 275-338, DSP voices as relocatable objects placed in free DSP L2, a second SRC page with four saved, p-lockable controls (stored in the sound record's spare slots 77 and 78; such projects still load on the stock OS), and since 2.6 a pattern service that reads and edits trigs and locks through the firmware's own editors. Building needs an elekloader with `sharc_raw` support for the Digitakt II (a branch of gdeo607's elekloader fork, proposed upstream). Do not flash 2.4, 2.5 or 2.6: they crash the unit at boot (I67).

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: an elekloader mod (core 2.6.1)); builds on `elekloader` (README: starts from core 1.0 (irpina's boot copier and hook bus, unchanged)); vendors `digikit` (README: adds the frameworks DigiKit's All-in-One builds its machines on); uses tool `digikit` (README: checked in the emulator) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README 2026-11-10, README (2026-11-11)_

### Digi2MacroOSC (MACRO)

MACRO, a macro-oscillator machine (type 11): 25 synthesis models and four DX7 patch banks after Emilie Gillet's Plaits, with a graphical model selector and HARM, TIMBRE, MORPH and MIX. Its DSP object is built from digikit's Plaits module. The README still names core-dt2 2.4, which crashes a unit at boot; use Digi2Core 2.6.1.

### Digi2ElixirPotionsDRUM (ELIXIR)

ELIXIR, a drum-synthesis machine (type 12) with four models picked by MODEL - DRUM, SNARE, CYMBAL, HIHAT - each with a pitch sweep and a transient; the voices follow the open-source LXR drum machine firmware (Sonic Potions / Erica Synths). Two SRC pages; host tests render sounds and fuzz the voice. Not together with older LXR test builds (same machine type). The README still names core-dt2 2.4, which crashes a unit at boot; use 2.6.1.

### Digi2String (STRING)

Alez22's Karplus-Strong STRING machine from the Digitakt mk1, ported to the Digitakt II: bowed, struck, noise-excited or plucked, with stiffness, excitation position, softness and a note-tracking tone filter. 0.2.0 makes STIFF and POS clearly audible, departing from the mk1 there. Needs Digi2Core 2.6.1 or later.

### Digi2Sophie (SOPHIE)

SOPHIE metallic percussion for the Digitakt II: Matt Estela's Sophie for Schwung, with PIPE and BOOM from soejrd's Sophie for Digitakt; FM and phase modulation with oscillator feedback, pitch sweep, bit crusher, drive and a resonant ring. Needs Digi2Core 2.6.1 or later. Overtone runs SOPHIE on the Digitone II.

### Digi2Digiseq (DIGISEQ)

Robbie's DIGISEQ sequencers for the Digitakt II: every track, audio or MIDI, picks a TYPE whose sequencer plays instead of its trigs - SNAKE (a path through a 4 x 2 grid), 185 (stage sequencer after ML-185), ARP (played by the track's own note trigs) and PRINT (writes the result as real trigs, with undo). Uses Digi2Core's pattern service; needs core 2.6.1 or later.

_Related: port of `digiseq-digitakt` (README: DIGISEQ for Digitakt by Robbie (ClaidArremer), adapted); mod for `elekloader` (README: built with elekloader); builds on `digi2core` (README: core-dt2 2.6.1 or later, its pattern service) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README 2026-11-10, README (2026-11-11)_

### Elektroid

Sample and SysEx manager. README device list includes Analog Heat MKI, MKII and +FX, Digitakt I and II, Digitone I/II/Keys, Syntakt (also Analog Four/Rytm/Keys, Model:Cycles/Samples, Monomachine MKII). GPL-3.0, 2,506 commits, 425 stars. No version/date visible.

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v3.4 (2026-08-22) adds Syntakt samples; also KORG logue and Monomachine; GPL-3.0-or-later; author's tool does not change firmware._

_Sources: GitHub README, lapin-list_

### Overwitch

Multitrack Overbridge audio on Linux. Supports Overbridge 2 devices incl. Analog Heat, Heat MKII and Heat +FX, Digitakt I/II, Digitone I/II/Keys, Syntakt. GPL-3.0, 671 commits. 2026-11-18 (README, docs/adding.md on main, no release yet): Overbridge 1 devices (Analog Four MKI, Analog Keys, Analog Rytm MKI) are supported with recent OS versions that speak the Overbridge 2 protocol (e.g. A4 MKI OS 1.56); only the Analog Four MKI is tested. Their track layout is set per device and can be written to the device from the GUI; their blocks hold 1 ms of audio (1-5 blocks, default 3).

_Latest seen (2026-10-31, secondary directories): altstrument: v2.2 (2025-12-21), GPL-3.0-or-later, JACK clients streaming multitrack Overbridge 2 audio._

_Related: builds on `dtdump` (README: based on the Overbridge USB reverse engineering in dtdump) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README, lapin-list, README, docs/adding.md (2026-11-18)_

### coldfire-rs

Rust stack for ColdFire V4e (MCF5441x): toolchain (rustc_codegen_gcc + libgccjit for m68k-elf), runtime, PAC generated from an SVD, and an Embassy HAL (GPIO, PIT, INTC, eDMA, UART, DSPI, eSDHC eMMC block reads, SSI/I2S, USB OTG device mode). Not an emulator and not an Elektron mod: the README never mentions Elektron or digikit, the only link is the topic tag "digitakt". It is relevant here because digikit names the MCF54415 as the control CPU of Digitakt II (and the Digitone II is described as ColdFire too). Drivers were run on the author's own MCF54415 board. README: API is young and may change before 1.0. 33 commits, Apache-2.0 OR MIT. Same owner also has deluge-sdk (Synthstrom Deluge, out of scope). Org shows no public members; no relation to ElekLabs/Em D found.

_Sources: GitHub README, FirestormAudio profile page_

### digi-roll-studio

Native Rust desktop sequencer for Digitakt II, Digitone II and Analog Four, built from digi-roll. Writes to hardware: README recommends throwaway projects. Safe-write ceremony of five rules (re-read and back up the destination pattern first, OS build on an allowlist, user confirmation, change only needed bytes, read back and byte-compare). Gen-2 dump protocol (digis) vs gen-1 (Analog Four). +Drive file-write commands 0x57/0x58/0x59 hardware-verified for a single chunk only, not called by the app (writes above 16 KiB refused); 0x5A/0x5B/0x5C (move/copy/delete) not implemented. Protocol code ported from elk-herd (BSD-2, (c) mzero). Fixtures: 34 real .syx dumps. 124 commits, GPL-3.0-or-later. Not firmware modding. Windows/Linux write testing incomplete. 2026-11-24 (v0.6.0/v0.6.1): Drum Steps, a 16-step grid editor beside the piano roll (paint, erase, velocity drag, per-track playheads); Kit Builder (K), a track grid and preset browser with filters, revert per track or for all auditioned tracks, a recovery backup kept even when verification fails; A4 writes keep the destination pattern's kit and refuse a blank pattern whose kit reference is unset (I201). A contributed Syntakt p-lock map (OS 1.42) is merged but enables no Syntakt writes. Saving a whole kit to the +Drive is planned for DN2 only.

_Related: vendors `elk-herd` (catalogue notes: protocol code ported from elk-herd) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: GitHub README, search 2026-10-31, tags v0.6.0/v0.6.1, README, PLAN, release notes, KIT-SAVE-WORK-PACKAGE, fixture and dump notes (2026-11-24)_

### digitakt-midi-mcp

MCP server to control a Digitakt II over MIDI (notes, CC, NRPN, transport, raw SysEx) over USB with Overbridge. Includes nrpn_constants.py (full NRPN list per README) and tests that need the physical unit; mappings rest on the manual and the author's code, no independent verification claimed. SysEx tools are experimental and "best-guess" - the README says Elektron has not published the pattern SysEx format. MIT, 46 commits, 11 stars. One of the few agent-facing Elektron tools; relevant model for how an agent can talk to a unit.

_Sources: GitHub README, search 2026-10-31_

### elk-herd

"Elektron device manager". Browser app in Elm for Digitakt and Digitakt II content over Web MIDI: whole-project transfer to and from device and files, reordering of patterns, sample pool and sound pool, renaming (altstrument 2026-11-03; development continues off GitHub, we do not link the new source location). Other projects call it the de-facto public documentation of Elektron's SysEx protocol (digi-roll-studio) and port its 7-bit SysEx codec and F0 00 20 3C framing (SYXGRID). BSD-2-Clause per those projects. The GitHub page is a stub: README says the project has migrated away from GitHub to an obfuscated address (not decoded by us) and that issues and pull requests generated by AI will be summarily rejected - do not open AI-generated ones. Device support is not stated on the stub; SYXGRID says elk-herd does not support the Digitone family; the Digitakt II entry is an inference from digi-roll (which ports its protocol for DT2/DN2). 70 stars.

_Sources: GitHub stub, digi-roll-studio README, SYXGRID README, altstrument (2026-11-03)_

### Elektron Emu

Five VST3 plug-ins (Mac, Windows) that run each machine's real OS in an emulated CPU: Digitakt II, Syntakt, Analog Rytm MKII, Digitone II, Model:Cycles. Firmware not included; the user places the .syx from Elektron's site in a per-machine folder. +Drive emulated and persisted; WAV loading on DT2, Rytm and DN2. Digitone II's DSP is compiled locally on first open (needs a C compiler, else a slow interpreter that renders offline only). Caveats: Rytm analog voices/effects are a custom model that does not sound like the real machine; Syntakt analog tracks 9-12 missing; Mac builds unsigned. 2 commits, 19 stars, no licence stated. Personal project, not affiliated with Elektron (panel photos belong to Elektron).

_Sources: GitHub README, altstrument tools page_

### dt2-capicola (Capicola time stretch for STRETCH/REPITCH/SLICE/GRID)

Custom OS that replaces the Digitakt II's native time-stretch and repitch DSP with an engine built on Heavylight Industries' Capicola (AGPL-3.0-or-later): covers STRETCH, REPITCH, SLICE and GRID; a CAPI parameter switches each track between the new engine and Elektron's; SLICE/GRID sync to tempo and BARS goes to 32. The GitHub repo did not answer on 2026-11-02 (deleted, renamed or private). Its 66 files are kept byte-exact in dt2-machine-lab under machines/capicola-reddit/upstream (pinned from a user-supplied zip, SHA-256 87bb2b07...), which builds its own overlay from it. A comment in its build script says digikit's flash cave 0x403117c4 froze the unit at the logo for that build; other projects use the cave on units (CONFLICTS O18).

_Related: builds on `keyframer-lab` (same Capicola keyframe engine by Heavylight Industries); cites `digikit` (catalogue notes: its build script comments on digikit's flash cave 0x403117c4) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

Closed-source browser app that preps audio and sends it over Web MIDI SysEx to the +Drive, with Transfer and +Drive Manager views and device profiles for Digitakt II, Digitakt, Analog Rytm (MKI/MKII) and Model:Samples. ### Mezclando (transition mode for Digitakt II)

A DJ-style mix mode on the SONG key: pick a reference pattern and bring its tracks, with their sequences and sounds, into the playing pattern one by one, with per-track levels, mutes and a one-step undo; YES loads the whole reference pattern with its kit (stock copy + paste). Uses only the firmware's own functions and stores nothing of its own; stock SONG functions move to FUNC + SONG and TRK + SONG. Built locally in a browser patch page or from source (m68k-elf GCC, Node 24, a Modwerk checkout with core-dt2 1.0). English and Spanish README. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-05.

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: NOTICE names elekloader (core-dt2 and its kit) as a base); builds on `modwerk` (README: build needs a Modwerk checkout with core-dt2 1.0); cites `digikit` (README: NOTICE credits digikit's research on the Digitakt II) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### digimod (Digitakt II mod builder)

A local web service (Docker, or native on macOS) that packs a Digitakt II .syx from ticked mods, checks it before download and, on a Mac, boots it in a built-in DT2 emulator. Mods: Polyphony (VOICES 1-8 per track, borrowing idle tracks' channels), Plaits (25 models and four DX7 banks on the DSP), Musical WAVE / Deja Vu, One-Shot Zoom and System Load; each mod's README says what was checked in the emulator and what on hardware. Notes that on hardware the DSP takes 7-12x longer than the emulator for one case. Also listed by altstrument. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-06.

_Related: vendors `digikit` (README credits: Plaits and other mods are ports of digikit work (AGPL-3.0-or-later)); vendors `digitakt-ii-research` (README credits: Musical WAVE / Deja Vu and One-Shot Zoom from Kari Gardarsson's All-in-One); uses tool `elektron-emu` (README: the emulator is built on xerydian's elektron-emu); uses tool `elektron-firmware-tool` (README: the firmware tool is by mischa85) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

### Whiplash (agent plays a Digitakt II)

A Hermes Agent plugin that jams on a Digitakt II over USB MIDI: starts patterns by genre or mood, changes sounds live by CC/NRPN, mutes tracks (optionally the unit's own mute, CC 94); nothing is saved to the unit. Falls back to a virtual MIDI port without hardware. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-06. 0.3.0-0.8.0 (CHANGELOG, 2026-11-11): the timing runs in the plugin's own sequencer on MIDI clock; parameter ramps, bar-aligned pattern edits, sample slot select (CC 19), a clock-only mode, melodies, chords and song arrangement, a mix tool, listening to the unit's USB audio, play-along and undo; it never sends SysEx or program change and writes nothing to the unit; caps of 48 ramps and 1,000 CC per second. 2026-11-20 (README, CHANGELOG 0.9.0-0.9.5, reference.md, hardware checklists): 0.9.0-0.9.5 (all 2026-11-19) add a named "ontology" library: grooves with five energy levels, microtiming and ghost notes, 28 named progressions, bass/stab/lead phrases that follow the chords, darker/brighter/tension intents and key changes, song forms and moves ("build to the drop in 16 bars"), a taste review, and six more genres (classic, progressive, minimal and tropical house, melodic and minimal techno); one new tool, whiplash_list_library. No new MIDI message type or CC number. None of it is tested on a Digitakt II; a v0.9 hardware checklist waits for a session. The multi-device studio plan moved to 0.10.

_Sources: GitHub search 2026-11-06, README, README (2026-11-12), CHANGELOG, README, CHANGELOG 0.9.0-0.9.5 (2026-11-20)_

### sample-shepherd

Organises a sample library (through Fourier Samples), exports it per device profile and syncs it to a sampler without breaking the projects on it: backs up projects, works out which samples they use, plans uploads and deletions and carries them out resumably; never deletes a sample a project uses. Elektron devices through elektroid-cli; used only with a Digitakt II so far (about 30,000 samples over a USB link measured at about 77 KB/s). Licence not stated. Found by GitHub search 2026-11-07. 2026-11-10: the CLI reports sync progress as JSON events and stops a sync cleanly between files, for a planned desktop app. 2026-11-11: `plan-edit` turns rows of a sync plan off or on by id. 2026-11-12: `library index` writes a read-only SQLite index of a library (path, category, duration, format, hash) for the desktop app's browser. 2026-11-13: library index --ratings fills each file's rating (keep, drop, misfiled) from Fourier's review file, read only. 2026-11-17 (app/README.md, docs): the desktop app's first piece exists in app/: a SvelteKit front end with a style sheet page; the Tauri shell and the CLI sidecar come next. Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-18 (docs/cli): `library ls` lists the indexed samples (with --json, one row event per sample for the app). Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-19 (docs, app/README): the app's first Library screen (folder tree, sample table, filters) reads a recorded library ls run. Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-20 (app/README, docs): the Library screen adds a "terrain" (folders as bands sized by sample count); the CLI refuses a --db that is not a library index. Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-21 (app/README, docs/cli): `export check --json` reports every issue a render would hit on the device (too many files in a folder, folders too deep, wrong rate or bit depth, Elektron names over 32 characters) as rows, and the app gains an Export check screen (shown with a digitakt_2_50_3 profile run). Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-22 (app/README, CLAUDE.md, desktop plan): the desktop app now has its Tauri shell (a native window around the screens, still reading recorded runs; the CLI sidecar comes next). Nothing new on the device side. 2026-11-23 (README, docs/fourier-patches): profiles digitakt_2_50_5 and generic_folder_5 sort up to five folder levels (a crowded group splits once more); not yet tried on a Digitakt. The project now carries 11 patches to the Fourier sorter. 2026-11-24 (app README, desktop plan): the desktop app gains a Sync plan screen (the plan's totals and two flows sized by bytes, export into the device and what's on the device to its fate; clicking a band filters the rows), fed by a recorded run until the sidecar exists. 2026-11-25: the desktop app gains a Device screen with a +Drive map (each sample sized by bytes, used and deleted ones marked), fed by the new `device listing --json` rows; free space waits for `device info` capacity.

### EUC+ (melodies for the Euclidean sequencer)

Adds Torso T-1-style generated melodies to the stock Euclidean sequencer: each Euclid hit gets a note from a pool of scale degrees in the pattern's KB SCALE and ROOT NOTE, moved by a phrase shape and a seeded, lockable random sequence. Own NOTES and RANDOM pages opened from the stock Euclid page; off by default per track; works on audio tracks (repitched) and MIDI tracks; patterns stay stock; settings are lost at power-off for now. Hooks the end of the audio and MIDI step fire (0x400d6e10, 0x400d7234 on OS 1.17). Built from your own OS file with shell scripts for Linux; a research log and a design document come with it. Credits Aggregat's rules and device facts for its build checks and flash procedure. Found via the owner 2026-11-08.

_Related: mod for `elekloader` (README: an Elekloader linkable mod (format 2), requires core-dt2 1.0); uses tool `digikit` (README: every EUC+ test runs in digikit's Digitakt II emulator); cites `mezclando` (commit 2026-11-08: Mezclando as prior art in docs/EXTENDED-EUCLID.md) - see [PROJECT-FAMILIES.md](PROJECT-FAMILIES.md)_

_Sources: owner 2026-11-08, README, mods/eucplus-dt2/mod.json, README (2026-11-11)_
